transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm just... having a hard time with some things lately. I've been trying to stay away from anything that reminds me of my old job. Like, I won't go near certain office buildings, and I definitely avoid networking events if they're near work sites. Even just... security talks. I don't know. And if anyone brings up the day it happened, I just... I make an excuse and leave. I can't talk about it.
Are there specific memories or thoughts about your old job that you try to avoid thinking about?

Well... yeah. Like I was just saying, I really just try to dodge anything to do with it. If a thought about... that day... pops into my head, I just push it away. I try to stay busy. That's why I stay away from those buildings and the talks and all that. I just don't want it in my head.
Have you been having any nightmares?

Yeah... sometimes. I guess. I mean, most nights I just lie there... tired, but I can't turn my brain off. And when I do fall asleep, I'll wake up from these dreams. Just... hearing the radios crackling, people shouting. Then I'm awake. Usually up way before the sun, just feeling like I didn't sleep at all.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving that day, like it's happening all over again?

I guess... yeah. Sometimes. It's just... out of nowhere. I'll be doing something normal, like washing dishes, or... driving past a warehouse gate. And it just pops back in my head. It's so sharp. I can hear the panic in people's voices. My chest gets all tight... like I'm right back there.
Do you try to avoid feeling certain emotions that remind you of what happened?
I don't know. I just... I try not to feel much of anything about it, I guess. I just want to move on.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself?
No. I don't think so. I mean... I'm just me. I don't really know what you mean by that.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats in your daily life?

I guess so. A little. It's just... when I walk into a meeting room at work, or a restaurant, I just like to see where the exits are first. And I usually pick a seat where nobody can come up behind me. I don't know... I just watch people's hands sometimes. It's just being careful, I think.
Do you find yourself jumping or startling easily when something unexpected happens, like a loud noise?

I suppose. Um... yeah. If a door slams, or a car backfires, I jump pretty hard. Or even if... somebody just touches my shoulder and I didn't see them coming. My heart starts racing. And it just... it keeps racing, long after everyone else has just moved on and forgotten about it. I don't know.
How long have you been avoiding things that remind you of your old job?
Um... a while. I guess it's been about... a year and seven months. Ever since they let me go, after... well, after that armed incident.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

I suppose. Um... yeah. Things like... listening to salsa music, or painting. Even just cooking Sunday dinner. They used to lift me up, but now... I don't know. I just sort of go through the motions. That good feeling just... it doesn't really come the way it used to.
Are there any activities that you used to find meaningful or enjoyable that you've lost interest in since the incident?
I think I just answered that. Um... yeah, the music and the painting. I just don't care much for them anymore.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened at your old job?
No... not really. I mean, I didn't cause it. It just... happened.
How much of your daily life would you say is affected by your efforts to avoid reminders of your old job?

A fair amount. Um... I've had to turn down interviews. And I stopped taking on volunteer things. It's just... I can't really get through meetings or site visits right now without needing to leave, or just... shutting down. So it's easier not to do them. 

Even with my family, or the mentoring groups I help with... people have started to notice. I just pull back now. I'm not leading things like I used to.
How many hours a day would you say you spend thinking about or trying to avoid reminders of your old job?
I don't really know. Um... I haven't kept track of the hours. It's just... hard to put a number on it.
Have you avoided forming close relationships with others since the incident at your old job?

I don't know about avoiding them... I still show up sometimes. For family things, or the mentoring. But... I don't feel close. It's like... I'm sitting behind glass. Just nodding along. They're all together, and I'm just... somewhere else.
Are there any activities that you used to find enjoyable, but now find you have no interest in at all?

I suppose so. Um... I used to really like painting. And listening to salsa music. Cooking Sunday dinner for the family, too. I still do them sometimes, but... I just kind of go through the motions now. It doesn't... lift me up, or feel good like it used to.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of your old job is something you do almost all the time, or is it something you can occasionally control or manage?

I guess it's... most of the time. I just try to stay away from anything that reminds me of it. Office buildings, networking events... even those security talks. I just dodge them. And if someone brings up that day... I just make an excuse to leave. I can't... I just don't want to deal with it.
Would you say that there are any situations or reminders of your old job that you are unable to avoid?
I don't think so. I mean... I just try to keep my distance from all of it. So I don't really run into things I can't get away from.
